summary: I anchored this research in the current official Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google prompting docs available on March 27, 2026, then used ACL/arXiv papers to check whether structural claims about ordering and formatting hold up empirically. The clearest cross-vendor pattern is that effective prompts are modular: stable role/rules in system or developer instructions, task-specific context and examples in user prompts, and explicit output contracts separated with tags or headings. Few-shot examples are most useful as a precision tool for format, tone, and edge cases, not as a universal default; order and formatting changes measurably affect model behavior, so prompt layout is not cosmetic. For machine-readable outputs, schema-constrained structured outputs are substantially more reliable than prompt-only JSON instructions.

findings.claim: Put durable behavior instructions in the system or developer layer, and keep request-specific details and examples in the user or task prompt.
findings.source: OpenAI Prompting guide (vendor-authored): https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompting ; Google system instructions intro (vendor-authored): https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/prompts/system-instruction-introduction
findings.evidence: OpenAI says overall tone or role guidance belongs in the system message while task-specific details and examples belong in user messages; Google says system instructions are processed before prompts and apply across turns.

findings.claim: Role or persona framing works best when it is short and concrete about expertise, task, and tone, rather than grandiose.
findings.source: Anthropic Claude prompting best practices (vendor-authored): https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices ; Google system instructions intro (vendor-authored): https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/prompts/system-instruction-introduction
findings.evidence: Anthropic says a one-sentence system role changes behavior; Google shows different role definitions produce clearly different responses for college versus primary-school audiences.

findings.claim: Prompt structure should be explicit and labeled: separate role, instructions, context, examples, constraints, and output format with headings or tags.
findings.source: Anthropic Claude prompting best practices (vendor-authored): https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices ; Google prompting strategies (vendor-authored): https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/prompting-strategies ; Google Vertex prompt design strategies (vendor-authored): https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/prompts/prompt-design-strategies
findings.evidence: Anthropic recommends XML tags to reduce misinterpretation; Google says ordering, labeling, and delimiters affect quality, and shows XML or Markdown templates with dedicated sections.

findings.claim: Constraint placement is strongest when stable behavioral rules are early or in system instructions, but long retrieved context should come first inside the task prompt and the actual question should come last.
findings.source: Google prompting strategies (vendor-authored): https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/prompting-strategies ; Anthropic Claude prompting best practices (vendor-authored): https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices
findings.evidence: Google recommends putting essential behavioral constraints, persona, and output requirements in system instructions or at the start of the prompt, while large context goes first and the specific question goes at the end. Anthropic reports up to 30% better response quality in long multi-document prompts when queries come last.

findings.claim: Write constraints as explicit, measurable requirements, not vague adjectives or mostly negative prohibitions.
findings.source: Google Vertex prompt design strategies (vendor-authored): https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/prompts/prompt-design-strategies ; Anthropic Claude prompting best practices (vendor-authored): https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices
findings.evidence: Google explicitly contrasts objective constraints like 3 sentences or less with vague requests like brief summary; Anthropic says to be specific about desired output format and constraints.

findings.claim: For reasoning-heavy tasks, start with zero-shot instructions and add few-shot examples only if the model still misses the desired format, edge cases, or tone.
findings.source: OpenAI reasoning best practices (vendor-authored): https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning-best-practices ; Anthropic Claude prompting best practices (vendor-authored): https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices ; Google few-shot examples guide (vendor-authored): https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/prompts/few-shot-examples
findings.evidence: OpenAI says to try zero-shot first and move to few-shot only if needed; Anthropic calls examples one of the most reliable steering methods; Google says few-shot improves reliability but still requires clear instructions.

findings.claim: When you use few-shot, examples should be relevant, diverse, consistently formatted, and explicitly marked as examples rather than mixed into instructions.
findings.source: Anthropic Claude prompting best practices (vendor-authored): https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices ; OpenAI prompt engineering guide (vendor-authored): https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-engineering ; Google few-shot examples guide (vendor-authored): https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/prompts/few-shot-examples
findings.evidence: Anthropic recommends 3 to 5 relevant, diverse, structured examples in example tags; OpenAI says examples should span diverse inputs and usually live in a developer message; Google says to use XML-like markup and consistent formatting.

findings.claim: Prompt layout is not cosmetic: formatting and order changes can materially change accuracy, so any structural edit should be evaluated like a code change.
findings.source: Sclar et al., arXiv 2023: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.11324 ; Pezeshkpour and Hruschka, NAACL Findings 2024: https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-naacl.130/ ; Cobbina and Zhou, EMNLP 2025: https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.1503/
findings.evidence: Sclar et al. report up to 76 accuracy-point swings from subtle prompt-format changes in few-shot settings. Pezeshkpour and Hruschka report 13% to 85% gaps when answer-option order changes. Cobbina and Zhou show predictions drift when demos, system prompts, and user messages are repositioned.

findings.claim: Few-shot examples can make prompts more robust, but they do not remove prompt sensitivity and can backfire if they conflict with the instructions or if you add too many.
findings.source: ProSA, EMNLP Findings 2024: https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-emnlp.108/ ; OpenAI reasoning best practices (vendor-authored): https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning-best-practices ; Google few-shot examples guide (vendor-authored): https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/prompts/few-shot-examples
findings.evidence: ProSA finds few-shot examples can alleviate prompt sensitivity. OpenAI warns that examples must align very closely with the instructions. Google warns that too few examples may not move behavior and too many can overfit.

findings.claim: For strict machine-readable output, prefer schema-constrained structured outputs or function calling over prompt-only requests such as respond in JSON.
findings.source: OpenAI structured outputs guide (vendor-authored): https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs ; Google structured output guide (vendor-authored): https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/structured-output ; Vellum production blog (vendor-authored, biased): https://www.vellum.ai/blog/we-dont-speak-json
findings.evidence: OpenAI says Structured Outputs ensures schema adherence, while JSON mode only guarantees valid JSON. Google says structured output gives predictable and parsable results. Vellum's production anecdote describes prompt-only JSON and few-shot JSON as still brittle in practice.

findings.claim: If you cannot use schema-constrained output, the most reliable prompt-only formatting pattern is to show the exact output shape with prefixes or a skeleton and then let the model complete it.
findings.source: Google prompting strategies (vendor-authored): https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/prompting-strategies ; OpenAI Prompting guide (vendor-authored): https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompting
findings.evidence: Google demonstrates an Output: prefix plus a partial JSON example to tighten formatting, and recommends structured prefixes in few-shot examples. OpenAI recommends concise YAML-style or bulleted example blocks so formats are easy to scan and reuse.

findings.claim: Agent instructions benefit from workflow scaffolding: define role, plan, constraints, context, output format, and an explicit validation pass instead of giving the model one undifferentiated paragraph.
findings.source: Google Vertex prompt design strategies (vendor-authored): https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/prompts/prompt-design-strategies ; Google prompting strategies (vendor-authored): https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/prompting-strategies ; OpenAI prompt engineering guide (vendor-authored): https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-engineering
findings.evidence: Google's sample template explicitly separates objective or persona, instructions, constraints, context, output format, few-shot examples, and recap, and also recommends planning and self-critique steps. OpenAI compares developer messages to function definitions and user messages to arguments, which supports this split for agent-style prompts.

gaps: I did not find strong 2024-2026 peer-reviewed work that isolates persona or role framing alone and quantifies its quality lift across broad real-world tasks; most current evidence there is vendor-authored.

Official Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google docs do not always expose stable on-page publication dates, so recency is based on the live documentation I accessed on March 27, 2026 rather than explicit page timestamps.
The empirical literature on constraint placement is strongest for prompt-order and formatting sensitivity, not for one universal best position across all model families and task types.
